source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"They are symptoms unrelated to schizophrenia because hallucinations and fixed false beliefs occur only in mood or neurologic disorders.","B":"They are psychotic symptoms of schizophrenia: hearing voices is a hallucination and fixed coded-message beliefs are delusional beliefs.","C":"They are exclusively cognitive symptoms because hallucinations and delusions primarily reflect deficits in attention, memory, and executive function.","D":"They are negative symptoms because hallucinations and delusions represent reductions in motivation, emotional expression, speech, and social engagement."}}
source_row.rationale: NIMH classifies hallucinations and delusions as psychotic symptoms of schizophrenia. Hearing voices is an auditory hallucination, and a fixed belief that strangers are sending coded television messages is delusional. Negative symptoms involve reductions such as diminished motivation or emotional expression; cognitive symptoms involve functions such as attention and memory.
source_row.source_detail: NIMH — Schizophrenia, Symptoms: psychotic symptoms include hallucinations, delusions, and thought disorder; negative symptoms and cognitive symptoms are separate categories. NIMH Schizophrenia publication revised 2024 and current in 2026; rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A client with schizophrenia reports hearing voices and believes strangers are sending coded messages through television programs. How should the nurse classify these findings?
